method: Deterministic, no-provider, virtual-time replay using production LeadCadence plus the 15-second minimum-spacing and safe-idle scheduling rules from src/index.ts. Events were read from the raw parent transcript; delegate streams were intentionally excluded because delegate settlements do not count toward this gate.

source.normalization: slim-replay export against the original parent initially stopped on a missing linked worker transcript (ENOENT). A private parent-only copy changed only the session-header cwd so the exporter would not follow worker pointers. Narrative records and timestamps were preserved; no worker settlement was counted.

costInterpretation.referenceOnly: Todo 049 cold catch-up used 3 provider calls across 2 update passes and cost $0.00784288 nominal. That is a two-pass cold-backlog sample, not a measured ordinary-update unit price.
costInterpretation.momProviderCallsPerUpdate: 1 proposal, with at most one repair call; thus 60 opportunities imply 60–120 provider calls in the stop-only scenario, before any cold-start catch-up.
costInterpretation.kev: Zero by default. If the optional advisor is configured, it screens ordinary batches only; compaction and explicit requests bypass it.

interpretation: Five/two/ten-minute coalescing yields about 14 ordinary updates per day in this busy session, plus compaction bypasses. It is far below per-message wakeups, but still a high update rate; the thresholds remain a starting point, not best practice.

The ten-minute age is not a hard maximum from the first event: one pending exchange never starts the timer. In this replay an isolated exchange waited up to 7.97 hours for a second exchange; once the second arrived, the batch flushed. A timer that expires while the lead is busy also waits for the next safe settlement.

Raw JSONL does not encode agent_settled events. The main estimate counts successful assistant stop records; the sensitivity includes error/abort terminal records. These are counterfactual call opportunities, not measured historical Mom calls.
